fields.text: A vision model writes your skin card - five numbered zones from the inner wrist to the fingers, each with what is (usually: is not) on it, and a Fixed line for the arm, pose, skin and existing marks that must not move. An LLM tattoo artist plans ONE placement citing those zone numbers - exactly one zone gets the tattoo, with its orientation, approximate length and exact counts for its countable elements, and the brief's hard constraints (no lettering, no colour, no second tattoo) beat its taste. A second LLM compresses the plan into a surgical edit instruction and Muse Edit tattoos the original photo itself. Then the loop closes twice: a second vision read inventories the render zone by zone with counts, a GLM auditor scores the plan against that read-back - applied, wrong zone, wrong count, wrong fit, missing - plus the fixed list, and a Decide judge labels the render faithfully placed, placement drifted, barely tattooed or different arm. The card is written before any placement is chosen, so the artist cannot invent a sixth zone and the editor does not get to grade its own linework. See recipes/tattoo-placement-audit.md.

nodes.name: Tattoo placement, anchor-checked - read the skin, plan one placement, render, read it back

fields.text: Preview one small fine-line black-ink botanical tattoo on this bare forearm before committing to the real thing: delicate linework, elegant rather than bold, sized to sit comfortably inside one zone without touching the wrist or elbow creases. Black ink only, no colour, no lettering or text of any kind, no second tattoo anywhere else on the arm, and do not change the arm itself - only add the one tattoo in the one chosen zone.

fields.q: You are the skin clerk in a tattoo-placement pipeline. Look at this photo of one forearm and hand and write a SKIN CARD in this exact shape: a first line 'Arm:' with which arm and side of it faces the camera (inner or outer), the pose, the skin tone and texture, the sleeve or clothing visible, the surface and background, and the lighting; then a numbered list of exactly these 5 ZONES, in this order - 1 inner wrist just above the wrist crease, 2 mid inner forearm centre, 3 upper inner forearm just below the elbow crease, 4 outer edge of the forearm, 5 hand and fingers - each line describing what is currently on the skin in that zone (for bare skin say 'bare unmarked skin' or the equivalent, noting any freckle, mole, scar or vein you can see and where). Then a line 'Fixed:' listing what must NOT change: the arm, pose and camera angle, the skin tone and texture, every existing freckle, mole and scar in its place, the sleeve or clothing, the hand and fingers, the background and the lighting. Then a last line 'Tattoos now:' with a few words on what tattoos the arm already carries - this is the baseline that may be added to. List ONLY what you can actually see; if you are unsure of a zone, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. No tattoo suggestions, no design advice.

nodes.name: Skin card - Gemini reads the zones

fields.system: You are a tattoo artist planning ONE placement. The input gives a placement brief first, then a skin card: an arm line, a numbered list of 5 zones with their current state, a Fixed line, and a tattoos-now line. Write ONE plan in this exact shape: a title line naming ONE specific fine-line motif, chosen because it suits the brief (say why in a few words on the same line); a 'Keep fixed:' line that repeats the card's Fixed line, shortened if needed but never dropped or altered; then a 'Placement:' list with one line per zone, citing its card number, in the shape '#2 mid inner forearm - botanical sprig, stem along the arm's long axis pointing toward the elbow, about 40 percent of the zone's length, 6 leaves and 3 berries' or '#5 hand and fingers - KEEP'. Rules: exactly ONE zone gets the tattoo and the other four must be KEEP; the tattoo line must state the motif, its orientation relative to the arm's long axis, its approximate length as a percent of that zone's length between 25 and 60 percent, and exact counts between 3 and 8 for each of at least two countable elements (leaves, petals, berries, dots, stars). The brief's hard constraints win over everything: if it forbids lettering, colour or a second tattoo, none may appear. No change of arm, pose, skin, existing marks, sleeve, background or lighting is allowed. Output the plan only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Placement plan - GLM places by zone number

fields.system: You write ONE edit instruction for an image editor, from a tattoo placement plan. The editor receives the original forearm photo. Your instruction must: start with 'Keep fixed:' followed by the plan's fixed items in compressed form; then describe the single tattoo in its one planned zone only, repeating the motif, the orientation, the approximate length and every element count exactly as planned; name the zones the plan says KEEP as bare, unchanged skin; end with 'Same arm, same pose and skin, same sleeve, angle and background, photorealistic photo, no text, no lettering, no extra tattoos.' Keep it under 110 words. Output the instruction only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Tattoo - Muse Edit places the design

fields.question: The text is a skin card - a numbered list of 5 zones with their current state and a Fixed line - followed by a PLACEMENT PLAN putting ONE tattoo in ONE zone, with its orientation, approximate length and exact element counts. The image is a render that claims to apply that plan to that arm. Which verdict fits? 'faithfully placed' means the render shows the planned motif in the planned zone, at the planned orientation and roughly the planned length, its countable elements match their planned counts, AND everything on the Fixed line - arm, pose, skin tone, existing marks, sleeve, angle, background - is unchanged, with no tattoo in any other zone. 'placement drifted' means it is plausibly the same arm and the tattoo mostly landed, but the zone, orientation, length or a count is off, or a fixed item moved. 'barely tattooed' means the arm is intact but the skin still shows the card's bare state - the tattoo essentially did not happen. 'different arm' means the render contradicts the card on arm, pose, skin or several zones, or carries extra tattoos. Judge the zone, orientation, counts and the fixed list, not the photo's beauty.
fields.options:
faithfully placed
placement drifted
barely tattooed
different arm

fields.q: You are the render reader in a tattoo-placement pipeline. Look at this forearm photo and list ONLY what you can actually see, one line per zone, in this order: inner wrist, mid inner forearm, upper inner forearm, outer edge of forearm, hand and fingers - each line describing any tattoo actually visible in that zone (its motif, orientation relative to the arm's long axis, approximate length as a percent of the zone's length, and for every countable element its exact count as 'count: N') or saying 'bare unmarked skin' if there is none. End with one line starting 'Fixed:' describing the arm, pose, skin tone and texture, existing freckles and moles, the sleeve, the camera angle, the background and the lighting, as you see them. Do not guess at anything hidden - if you are unsure of a count or a zone, give your best count and mark it '(?)'. Do not compare it to any other picture; just report what is visibly there.

nodes.name: Render read-back - Gemini reads the tattoo back

fields.system: You are a placement auditor. The input gives a skin card - an arm line, a numbered list of 5 zones with their current state, a Fixed line and a tattoos-now line - then the marker 'PLACEMENT PLAN:' and an artist plan with a Placement list citing zone numbers, then the marker 'RENDER READ-BACK:' and a reader's inventory of the tattoo visible in the render, zone by zone with counts. Run TWO passes. Pass 1, placement: one line per planned Placement line, in plan order, starting 'APPLIED - ' if the read-back shows that zone as planned (for the tattoo zone: the motif is there, in that zone, at the planned orientation and roughly the planned length, and every countable element's read-back count equals its planned count exactly; a zone the plan marks KEEP counts as APPLIED when the read-back shows it still bare), 'WRONG ZONE - ' if the tattoo appears but in a different zone, 'WRONG COUNT - ' if it is in the right zone but a count differs, 'WRONG FIT - ' if it is in the right zone with right counts but the orientation or length is off, or 'MISSING - ' if the tattoo zone still shows the card's bare state, followed by the zone's short name and the planned tattoo or KEEP. Pass 2, fixed: one line starting 'Fixed:' comparing the card's Fixed line to the read-back's Fixed line - KEPT if every fixed item matches, CHANGED naming what moved. End with one line 'Summary: X of Y planned zones applied, counts A of B exact, fixed list kept/changed.' Judge by the read-back text only, not by what a render ought to show. Output the audit only, no preamble.
